prompt:
Create ONE production 2D game sprite ANIMATION ATLAS. Exactly 16 genuinely sequential frames in a precise 4-column by 4-row UNIFORM grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. ONE complete creature in EVERY cell, fixed side view facing LEFT. A genuine transparent ALPHA background. Keep at least 12% blank padding inside every cell on ALL sides, including all weapon tips, feet, tails, coral and tentacles. Choose ONE global drawing scale that fits the LARGEST pose; never normalize each pose bbox, never crop body or weapon. Stable pelvis/stance root in each equal cell, with only the action's natural weight shift. Same camera, line weight, anatomy, costume and material volume in all 16 drawings. Match the reference's weathered marine bone/skin/cloth, dark-fairytale hand-painted rendering, restrained ivory/grey-teal palette and tiny amber accents. No labels, text, frames, grid lines, scenery, ground patch, baked shadow, detached projectile, glowing trails, aura or effects. Do NOT add limbs, swap weapon hand, change weapon type or repeat the same pose with only texture noise.
IDENTITY: The stocky armored amphibious beam guard in the reference: low skull-like ivory head crest, amber eye, layered dark slate shoulder plates, broad clawed feet, muted purple waist cloth and a broad CURVED CRESCENT bone blade on a short wooden haft. Keep two arms and two legs and the same hand grips. Do not substitute a straight spear.
ACTION: The character anticipates a defense counter slash: brace the crescent against an imagined hit, compress the shoulder and wrist while the feet stay planted, rotate the weapon grip; snap a short fierce LEFT returning crescent strike; follow through and recover behind the raised blade.
TIME ORDER: frames1�C6 clearly reveal neutral��plant/load��joint bend��further body/weapon retraction��strong anticipation��maximally loaded ready pose. Frames7�C10 release the described action with four clear intermediate moving poses; frames11�C16 show followthrough��deceleration��partway recovery��weight returns��weapon/limbs reset��ready stance. Maintain continuous mechanical/anatomical attachments. We will separately map these phases onto a real game's existing preparation, contact and recovery windows, so NO hit flash or attack effect may be baked into the preparation body. Intended in-game body height about100px: prioritize clear silhouette and weapon grip over excessive tiny detail.
CRITICAL: reference background is NOT part of the character. All blank space outside the figure must be literally fully transparent ALPHA ZERO, NOT semi-transparent white, NOT cloud texture, NOT an opaque white sheet. Character-only die-cut sprites on completely empty alpha. Draw each creature smaller, at most60% cell height/width including the complete weapon, so no weapon or foot touches cell edge. ONE existing staff/axe and exactly TWO hands holding it, no spare poles. Full body and weapon tips in every cell.
